survey: A saguaro-style cactus stands upright in rolling sand with a few pebbles, against a flat orange diamond-pattern backdrop. Main trunk: a vertical ribbed cylinder with a rounded dome top. It is seen nearly level from slightly above. Its vertical ribs bunch together toward the left and right edges as the surface turns away, and they come together at the dome. A small pink flower sits on the crown and is seen slightly from above, which fits the view. Left arm: a horizontal elbow leaves the trunk's left side low down and turns up into a shorter vertical column with a dome tip. Right arm: a horizontal elbow leaves the right side higher up and turns up into a taller column. On both arms the ribs run along the elbow and then turn vertical, and both upright columns stay parallel to the trunk. The spines are small cones spread along the ribs and get smaller toward the silhouette edges. Contact: the trunk goes into the sand along a gently curved base line, which is what a cylinder looks like from slightly above. The sand plane and the pebbles' top faces are seen from the same moderately raised camera. The ground plane, trunk, arms and flower all agree on one viewpoint, and the verticals stay vertical.
